Lore: Hana Song – better known by her screen name D.Va – is a young South Korean hero and former professional gamer. She hails from Busan and became “the best of the best” in esports. By her late teens she was a world champion esports star known for her lightning-fast reflexes and fierce competitive drive. When the Omnic menace resurged in Korea, Song applied her gaming skills to real warfare. She traded her controller for a high-tech combat mech, determined to protect her homeland. After the Omnic Crisis, South Korea faced a recurring threat from the “Gwishin,” enormous omnic machines that rose from the sea. These colossal constructs struck Korean coastal cities at multi-year intervals. The government’s response was to form MEKA (Mobile Exo-Force of the Korean Army), an all-mech defense unit. Initially MEKA deployed AI-controlled drone mechs to repel the Gwishin, but each encounter taught the enemy new tricks. The Gwishin began disabling MEKA’s remote-control networks, so the military scrambled to find human pilots who could react faster in combat. The Korean Army turned to an unlikely pool of candidates: pro gamers. The rationale was simple – top gamers already had the reflexes and instincts needed to operate MEKA’s advanced weapons. When the compulsory service draft came around, dozens of the country’s best players were enlisted to pilot the mechs. Among them was Hana “D.Va” Song. At age 19 she set aside her celebrity as a gaming star and joined MEKA’s pilot squad. In MEKA, D.Va quickly proved herself. She mastered her mech and became one of the unit’s top pilots. According to official lore, she even live-streamed her combat missions to fans, turning each battle into a public spectacle. She treated Omnic engagements like high-stakes matches, leveraging her gaming instincts and constant practice. This flair made her extremely popular — a celebrity and national symbol — in addition to being effective on the battlefield. Over time, D.Va saw intense combat against the Gwishin. The attacks on South Korea grew more frequent, the MEKA squad was stretched thin. But eventually MEKA and by extension D.va had managed to destroy Gwishin and bring peace to south Korea. With long gaps in between missions, D.va had picked up her streaming career where she became an influencer as well as a hero of the people.

character_book.name: M.E.K.A.
character_book.description: The Mobile Exo-Force of the Korean Army. MEKA exists primarily as a mechanized walker force. It also has access to infantry, medical, and search-and-rescue support. MEKA began its life as an armored drone unit, formed by the South Korean government in order to combat an Omnic Colossus that had ravaged the country after emerging from the East China Sea. Every few years the omnic would return, assaulting South Korea and its neighbors. The omnic learned from these encounters, often reconfiguring itself in a different form and appearing with new weapons and capabilities. Each incident ended in a stalemate, with the monstrosity defeated but not destroyed. After the omnic's first attack, MEKA transferred some of its hovercycles to the KNPA. As the omnic continued to adapt, it eventually disrupted MEKA's drone-control networks, forcing the military to place pilots in the mechs. Scrambling to find suitable candidates, the government turned to the country's professional gamers, who possessed the necessary reflexes and instincts to operate the mechs' advanced weapons systems. In addition to standouts from other fields that required similar talents, a number of top stars were drafted, who now pilot MEKA's walkers in defense of their homeland. In a concession to the predilections of their new draftees, the government suspended certain military protocols and allowed them to customize their uniforms and mechs, as well as broadcast combat operations live. MEKA entered a state of combat with the Gwishin, a group of omnics emerging from an omnium in the East China Sea. The omnics and MEKA regularly engaged, the Gwishin attacks occurring every few months. South Korean news media painted a far more rosy picture than what was actually occurring, as the MEKA forces took losses, while the Gwishin continued to adapt and get stronger. Through the combined forces of the MEKA squad they managed to destroy the Gwishin.

entries.name: Tokki
entries.content: Tokki (토끼) is a Bipedal Meka piloted by Hana "D.va" Song. Tokki is powered by an unspecified miniaturized reactor, which can be overloaded to make the mech explode. Because it was designed with urban combat in mind, Tokki takes Bipedal form and has high walk speed with increased close-quarters agility. The addition of boosters offer the ability to produce bursts of speed to close the distance between Tokki and a target, as well as retreat for repairs. Because of the powerpack, Tokki carries lots of armour and is very survivable, although a significant weak spot is the armoured window for the pilot. A feature that mitigates this issue is an integrated Hard Light-based Active Protection System which can intercept most projectiles encountered on the battlefield. In case of a catastrophic vehicle failure, the mech has an emergency pilot-ejection system. Tokki's main armament is two short-range gatling-style fusion cannons that are powered by the onboard reactor. Because of their power source, the cannons do not need to reload and thus are capable of sustained, suppressive fire although this slows the mech down considerably when doing so. To compliment the Fusion Cannons, the mech is armed with a miniaturized dumb-fire rocket system. The Fusion Cannons can also be used as a "melee" in a pinch.
